title: Bookings and Search Quality of Life
lede: Operators keep their place in Bookings, can begin a reservation from every Bookings context, and can recover Search without discarding trustworthy same-query results.

stats.n: Query, filters, sort, page, and view are URL-backed
Permission-aware page action across all tabs and scopes
Bookings, Search, debounce, realtime, and mutation contracts

changes.h: Opening a booking lost list context
changes.was: Pagination lived only in component state, URL rehydration reset the page, and card/table preference was not part of browser history.
changes.now: The complete list context is serialized through App Router replacement navigation and rehydrates on browser Back. Clear all also clears the search query.

changes.h: Reservation creation depended on the selected tab
changes.was: The action lived inside reservation-list rendering and disappeared in other Bookings contexts.
changes.now: One permission-aware New reservation action stays in the Bookings page header across tabs and active/past scope.

changes.h: Search failures were a dead end
changes.was: Complete and partial failures explained the problem but offered no direct retry; a failed refresh could also discard a previously healthy result group.
changes.now: Complete and partial failure states offer Retry. Same-query rows from a failed source remain visible until that source successfully refreshes, while a new query never inherits stale rows.

verification: Focused tests: 37 passing across six Bookings and Search contract files.
Docs: codemaps are current and npm run verify:docs passes.
notes: No before/after screenshot pair is claimed. The required isolated authenticated Playwright identity is unavailable: PLAYWRIGHT_EMAIL, PLAYWRIGHT_PASSWORD, and PLAYWRIGHT_ROLE are unset, and no saved storage state exists. This blocks honest same-account, same-data desktop and narrow-width capture.
No API, schema, permission, reservation lifecycle, custody, deployment, or production-data behavior changed.
